jobs.jd: If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/If you are interested in this position, please apply on Twitch's Career site https://www.twitch.tv/jobs/en/ About Us Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day. We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. We’re on a quest to empower live communities, so if this sounds good to you, see what we’re up to on LinkedIn and X, and discover the projects we’re solving on our Blog. Be sure to explore our Interviewing Guide to learn how to ace our interview process. About the Role We're looking for a data scientist with strong statistics and modeling skills to be the science partner for the machine learning and recommendation systems behind Twitch's discovery products. You will work with product managers, ML engineers and applied scientists to help build what our recommendation systems should optimize for. That means balancing what a viewer does today (a click, a play, minutes watched) against what keeps them coming back: return visits, daily habits, and lasting connections with creators. It also means weighing short-form clips against long-form live content, and each surface against the others. This role will draw from a variety of statistical learning techniques, causal inference, optimization and recommender systems evaluation, and it still owns the full path from question to decision. Reporting to the Director of Data Science, you will work from our San Francisco, CA office. You Will - Help define the objective functions and success metrics for ranking and recommendations across feeds, search and notifications. Make the trade-offs explicit between short-term engagement (clicks, plays, watch time) and long-term outcomes (return visits, retention, new creator connections), including how short-form clips and live content add to or take away from each other. - Evaluate ranking, recommendation and feed changes with ML engineers and applied scientists. This covers A/B tests and long-running holdouts, offline metrics that predict online results, and the cost and value of exploration and cold start. Handle the hard cases: novelty effects, interference between experiments, two-sided marketplace effects involving creators and viewers, and feedback loops in recommendation data. - Build statistical and ML models that explain viewer behavior and size opportunities, such as propensity, uplift, survival and retention models. Include proxy metrics that predict long-term retention, so teams can decide in days rather than months. - Turn ambiguous product questions into clear analyses. Quantify the uncertainty, and make recommendations that inform the machine learning and discovery roadmap. - Define the logging and data needed to measure discovery surfaces, and check its quality. - Contribute to the team's standards for experimentation, causal inference and model evaluation, and share what you learn with other data scientists. Perks - Medical, Dental, Vision & Disability Insurance - 401(k) - Maternity & Parental Leave - Flexible PTO - Amazon Employee Discount About the team Twitch is all about community, and our Community team is a core pillar of what makes Twitch, Twitch. Community Discovery & ML (CDML) helps millions of viewers find the creators and communities they'll love. That covers search, browse, the mobile live and clips feeds, recommended notifications, and the recommendation systems behind them. When a viewer finds a new creator through one of these, it's often the start of a lasting connection. That connection is what keeps viewers, and the creators they watch, coming back. - 3+ years of data scientist experience - A BA/BS in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, Data Science or a related quantitative field, or equivalent industry experience. - 3+ years as a data scientist in a high-velocity, data-driven environment, with hands-on experience applying statistical modeling and machine learning (regression, classification, causal inference, time series), including the assumptions behind each method and when it fails. - Experience designing and analyzing online experiments, including variance reduction, power analysis and the pitfalls of interpreting results. - Expert SQL and proficiency in Python or R. - A track record of using data and models to influence product decisions and leadership. - An MS or PhD in a quantitative field. - Experience with recommender systems, search ranking or feed ranking, such as offline evaluation (precision and recall, NDCG), exploration versus exploitation, or cold-start problems. - Experience with multi-objective optimization or with defining objective functions for ranking systems, including choosing weights between competing goals. - Experience building proxy metrics for long-term outcomes, or estimating long-term effects from long-running holdouts or observational data (e.g., difference-in-differences, synthetic control, uplift modeling). - Experience with two-sided platforms or marketplaces, where changes for viewers also affect creators or supply. - Experience on a consumer content platform: streaming, short-form video, social or marketplaces. - Familiarity with Twitch, as a viewer or a creator (or both!). jobs.title: Compiler Engineer - Machine Learning Compiler
jobs.jd: About us Mythic is building the future of AI computing with breakthrough analog technology that delivers 100× the performance of traditional digital systems at the same power and cost. This unlocks bigger, more capable models and faster, more responsive applications—whether in edge devices like drones, robotics, and sensors, or in cloud and data center environments. Our technology powers everything from large language models and CNNs to advanced signal processing, and is engineered to operate from –40 °C to +125 °C, making it ideal for industrial, automotive, aerospace, and defense. We’ve raised over $100M from world-class investors including Softbank, Threshold Ventures, Lux Capital, and DCVC, and secured multi-million-dollar customer contracts across multiple markets. About the role Join us in building the next generation of AI compilers. You’ll play a key role in developing the compiler for our novel AI accelerator, working side-by-side with hardware engineers and ML researchers. Your work will shape how deep learning workloads run on cutting-edge dataflow hardware—defining the instruction set, execution model, and developer experience. The result: a compiler that delivers breakthrough performance while remaining seamless and intuitive for ML developers. Here's what you will do Contribute across the full compiler stack, including operator lowering, graph/IR transformations, optimization passes, and backend code generation Optimize for dataflow architectures, developing pipelined schedules, memory orchestration, and resource-constrained execution strategies Collaborate with hardware architects to influence architectural features, ensuring the compiler and hardware evolve together Develop compilation strategies that unify our analog compute with digital subsystems Build and maintain a compiler that produces high-performance binaries with strong debugging support, clear error messages, and predictable performance models Here's the background we hope you will have 3+ years of experience building compilers or high-performance systems software, especially those involving complex resource management or optimization. Expert in modern C++ (C++14/17/20) and strong Python. Experience with compiler IRs (SSA-based or graph-based), transformations, and code generation Exposure to specialized accelerators (GPU, NPU, FPGA, or custom ASIC) or parallel architectures The following would be nice to have, but is not required Experience with machine learning compiler stacks (e.g., ONNX, MLIR, TVM, XLA, IREE, PyTorch), with contributions to MLIR or LLVM projects a plus Experience with optimization methods (LP/MIP, CP, SAT/SMT) using solvers like Gurobi or OR-Tools for scheduling and resource allocation Experience compiling for specialized accelerators (GPU, NPU, FPGA, or custom ASIC) on DNN workloads; GPU/DSP experience is valuable if combined with compiler backend work beyond kernel tuning Familiarity with heterogeneous compilation, especially mixing custom accelerators with CPUs/GPUs/NPUs, and exposure to analog or in-memory compute is a plus Experience collaborating in compiler–hardware co-design (architecture + ISA) for better compiler usability and hardware efficiency What we offer The opportunity to shape how deep learning and LLM workloads are compiled on novel hardware. A role that spans software and hardware co-design, shaping both the compiler and the accelerator architecture A collaborative, innovative team that values engineering rigor, continuous integration, and user-focused design. We foster an environment of shared learning and technical excellence Competitive compensation, equity, and benefits package Compensation Additional Information At Mythic, we foster a collaborative and respectful environment where people can do their best work. We hire smart, capable individuals, provide the tools and support they need, and trust them to deliver. Our team brings a wide range of experiences and perspectives, which we see as a strength in solving hard problems together. We value professionalism, creativity, and integrity, and strive to make Mythic a place where every employee feels they belong and can contribute meaningfully.

jobs.jd: Today, NVIDIA is tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. As an NVIDIAN, you'll be immersed in an inclusive, encouraging environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how we can make a lasting impact on the world. We are looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join our new User Simulation and Advanced Synthetic Data Generation team. You will own the systems our research runs on: the architecture, scale, and releases of our open-source framework. You'll also build the environments where simulated users meet models and agents. User simulation is quickly becoming core infrastructure for evaluating and training AI models and agents. They are judged by how they work with users, people or other agents, over many turns: holding a conversation, using tools, or collaborating on code in a real repository. Real data is thinnest here: slow and costly to collect, skewed toward existing users, and missing the long tail of languages, domains, and safety scenarios. We build grounded synthetic users and simulators, then use both to find capability gaps and close them with targeted training data and RL environments. A lot of our work ships as open source, including NeMo User Sim, Nemotron-Personas, and the data and environments we generate. We build our own systems on these same tools. We publish and present at top conferences, and we organize UserSim @ NeurIPS 2026, the first NeurIPS workshop on user simulation. The team serves three groups: Internal partners , including Nemotron and other model, agent, and product teams who evaluate and train their models with our simulators. Open-source users and contributors who build on the framework for their own models, agents, and languages. The research community , through work that pushes the state of the art and is published at top venues. The mission is the boss. We organize around the problem, not titles or ownership. Researchers write production code, engineers shape research, and everyone works directly with partner teams. We share credit, review each other's work candidly, and pick up whatever moves the mission forward. What you'll be doing: Own the architecture of NeMo User Sim: the conversation engine, configuration-driven pipelines, and extension API. Scale simulation to tens of thousands of concurrent multi-turn episodes against hosted and self-served models (e.g., vLLM, NIM), sharded across Slurm or Kubernetes. Runs must survive rate limits and partial failures, resume cleanly, and reproduce down to the row. Build and run environments for agents. These include stateful simulated tool services, and sandboxed coding environments where simulated users work with coding agents on real repositories. Verifiers and hidden tests grade the results. Connect simulated users to NeMo Gym and RL training, and keep the loop fast and cheap. Turn research prototypes into reliable, tested features together with research scientists. Run the open-source project: versioned releases, CI/CD, dependency and license hygiene, issue triage, and contributor reviews. Build the pipelines behind our open data releases, onboard internal partner teams, and present the framework at conferences. What we need to see: BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience). 6+ years building production ML systems, data pipelines, or developer libraries. Expert Python skills, with a track record of typed, tested libraries that other teams depend on. Experience running LLM workloads at scale: serving (e.g., vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, NIM), concurrency, and cost. Experience with LLM evaluation, training-data pipelines, or agents that use tools. Strong software design judgment on interfaces, versioning, and backward compatibility, with the mission ahead of ownership and credit. Ways to stand out from the crowd: Maintaining a widely used open-source ML library. RL training infrastructure or environments, such as NeMo Gym or NeMo RL. Infrastructure for coding agents: container sandboxes and SWE-bench-style harnesses. Inference optimization: distillation, quantization, or speculative decoding. Experience with NeMo Data Designer, Ray, or Spark and experience with multilingual text processing, such as language identification, scripts, and localization. Co-design and optimize agentic systems across NVIDIA's software and hardware stack, from models and inference through compilers, runtimes, libraries, kernels, and GPUs. Demonstrate measurable improvements in correctness, performance, or developer productivity. Take ideas from research prototype to production: own technical directions end to end, set a high bar for rigor, and work with partner teams to deliver them into NVIDIA products. What we need to see: Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience. 6+ years of relevant industry or research experience (including PhD research) in AI systems, agentic AI, machine learning, reinforcement learning, compilers, high-performance computing, or computer architecture. Hands-on research or development experience in agent systems, coding agents, model training, reinforcement learning, or modern AI inference systems. Strong Python programming skills and proficiency in C/C++ or Rust, with solid software engineering fundamentals. Experience with GPU programming and performance optimization using CUDA or comparable accelerator platforms, and the ability to work effectively across system boundaries. Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd: PhD research in a relevant area, with demonstrated ability to formulate research questions, build working implementations, and evaluate them rigorously. Track record of building high-impact coding agents, autonomous software-engineering systems, developer tools, or agent training and evaluation environments. Hands-on experience with GPU performance optimization, or with optimizing and deploying on TRT-LLM, SGLang, vLLM, or Transformer Engine. Evidence of technical depth and ownership through impactful research prototypes, deployed systems, benchmark results, or substantial open-source contributions. Relevant publications are welcome; we especially value strong engineering and measurable real-world impact. With highly competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package, NVIDIA is widely considered to be one of the technology industry's most desirable employers. We have some of the most brilliant and hardworking people in the world working with us and our product lines are growing fast in some of the hottest state of the art fields such as Virtual Reality, Artificial Intelligence, Deep Learning and Autonomous Vehicles. Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary range for this position is 187,500 USD – 364,000 USD. jobs.title: Applied AI Engineer, Mid-Market Enterprise
jobs.jd: About the Team OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineeriIng teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works. Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere. About the Role As a Mid-Market Enterprise Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations. This is a rare opportunity to work as one of the early hires for a new segment within Applied AI Engineering, contributing real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve. This role is based in our SF or NYC office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Partner directly with enterprise customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria. - Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes. - Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators. - Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance. - Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution. - Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact. - Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback. - Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments. You’ll thrive in this role if you: - Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting. - Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or production engineering—not only program or stakeholder management. - Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable. - Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment. - Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost. - Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes. - Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives. - Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments. - Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. jobs.jd: To get the best candidate experience, please consider applying for a maximum of 3 roles within 12 months to ensure you are not duplicating efforts. Job Category Sales Job Details About Salesforce Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all. Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce. What You’ll Be Doing & Why It Matters The architect team has four domains that together make the platform work for customers: Platform Advantage, Emerging Tech & UI Innovation, Data & AI Excellence, and Governance & Trust. This role sits in Governance & Trust, which covers identity, security, and audit. Agents now take actions, call tools, and work with other agents, often across systems Salesforce doesn’t own. Each step prompts the same questions from a customer’s security and risk leaders: who is this agent acting as, what can it touch, who approved it, and how do we stop it? You answer those questions with architecture, not assurances. When an AI program reaches the security review, the risk committee, or the Chief Information Security Officer, you show how identity, data access, agent authority, and audit work, and what it takes to prove it. You start from the customer’s risk and business problem, not a product pitch. You stay engaged until the controls are in place, because trust is what lets AI scale. Core Responsibilities & Scope Design agent identity and access architecture: agents as first-class identities, least privilege, Open Authorization (OAuth) scoping, and a clear chain back to an accountable human Advise on data security and privacy, including sharing and field-level access, encryption, masking, residency, and backup and retention Define agent guardrails, runtime control, observability, and audit using the Einstein Trust Layer, deterministic controls, human-in-the-loop, governance of external agents, event monitoring, agent session tracing, and security information and event management (SIEM) integration Lead AI governance and risk work, including risk tiering, approval gates, and regulatory readiness, while aligning C-suite stakeholders and working with pre-sale and post-sale teams to resolve platform-fit questions for customers Minimum Requirements 5+ years in enterprise or solutions architecture, with direct experience influencing senior technical and business stakeholders and staying engaged through delivery, including recovering stalled work Deep expertise in at least one of the five focus areas above, enough to be the final word in a room Fluency across the Salesforce platform or adjacent security, identity, or governance technology, and experience using AI tooling to build solutions and work more efficiently B.S., M.S. or PhD in Computer Science, Software Engineering or MIS Preferred Qualifications Working knowledge of the other architect domains, enough to know when to hand off Hands-on experience with Shield, Security Center, or the trust controls in Agentforce and MuleSoft Security or AI governance certifications or Salesforce Architect credentials Strong visual communication skills for architecture storytelling Unleash Your Potential When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best . Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Apply today to not only shape the future — but to redefine what’s possible — for yourself, for AI, and the world. Growth at Private Equity Insights

Are you looking master the latest AI tools, build agents, and put them to work on real business problems? Are you the person who gets things done and gets their hands dirty? If so, now is the time to apply for the AI Implementation role at Private Equity Insights.

If you want an ambitious mission, real ownership and the fastest learning curve of your career: apply.

Private Equity Insights is the world’s largest Private Equity community with 1m PE professionals, delivering impact through 12 global PE conferences with thousands of the world’s best investors and operators such as Blackstone, BlackRock, Apollo, Carlyle, CVC, KKR, and many more.

  • Unlimted AI Tokens We are ready to invest in AI and will equip you with all the tools and accesses you need to create 1000x results
  • Master the highest bar in the world. Our audience is the world's most demanding investors. They ignore anything average. If your work can make them act, you can make anyone act.

  • A UK work permit. We do not sponsor visas.

  • Exceptional drive and desire to be the best at what you do

Full-time, in person from our London office (WeWork), 5 days a week. Expect to travel for work about 20 days a year. The start date is flexible.

NVIDIA's GPU runs Deep Learning algorithms, simulating human intelligence, and acts as the brain of computers, robots, and self-driving vehicles that can perceive and understand the world. Our team is building the machine learning backbone of the Perception component for NVIDIA DRIVE AV. We are seeking the best Machine Learning Engineers with a background in computer vision, LiDAR & camera perception, multi-sensor fusion and AI infrastructure who are passionate about solving the hardest problems for self-driving cars. Are you interested in inventing human-level AI for perception under real world conditions? If so, join us! What You'll Be Doing: Model Development: Design, train, and optimize innovative machine learning models for LiDAR/camera perception and multi-sensor fusion (e.g., object detection/classification, image classification, semantic segmentation, tracking). Develop and coordinate entire ML workflows, covering data pipelines, model training, model metrics, continuous performance instrumentation, and reporting. Productization: Take ML models and algorithms from initial evaluation and experimentation all the way to product level on the NVIDIA DRIVE AV platform, developing highly efficient product code in C++. Innovation: Keep track of the latest developments in machine learning, and incorporate techniques that improve platform performance. Collaborate with LiDAR/camera teams, developers, engineers, and managers to turn complex ideas into reliable solutions for autonomous driving. What We Need to See: MS or PhD in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience. 8+ years of relevant proven industry experience applying machine learning to address real-world problems. Strong C++ and Python programming and debugging skills with experience in developing for large, complex systems. Deep practical experience applying machine learning to lidar/camera perception and multi-sensor fusion in automotive or related fields. Experience with deep learning frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow) and a strong understanding of the mathematical foundations of ML. Building and sustaining training and essential metric workflows for large-scale datasets. Excellent communication and analytical skills. Self-motivated drive to solve hard problems. Ways to Stand Out From the Crowd: Multi-sensor fusion, LiDAR or Camera Perception Experience: Proven track record of developing and shipping deep learning models for LiDAR/Camera and Multi-Sensor Fusion in a production environment. Advanced Model Knowledge: Familiarity with modern network architectures like Transformers and their application to visual recognition tasks. AV Production Experience: A history of delivering ML features and models into a production autonomous vehicle stack or a related robotics product. Performance Optimization: Experience with model optimization for real-time inference on embedded or automotive platforms (e.g., using TensorRT). We believe that realizing self-driving vehicles will be a defining contribution of our generation (e.g., traffic accidents are responsible for ~1.25 million deaths per year worldwide). We have the funding and scale, but we need your help on our team. jobs.title: Sr Applied Scientist, Embedded Battery Algorithms, Energy Storage
jobs.jd: Do you want to write the algorithms that control next-generation batteries, and shape the future of energy storage? This role sits where electrochemistry, data/ML, and control theory meet. You will develop the physics-informed and data-driven methods that estimate state of charge, health, power capability, and remaining life, and validate them against lab and fleet data until they are ready to ship. Your algorithms will decide how hard a battery can be pushed, when it needs attention, and how long it will last, so they shape the safety, warranty, and economics of the whole product. You will work side by side with cell, systems, and software engineers, and as an early hire you will help define how we develop and validate battery algorithms. This role can be based in Boston, Irvine, Sunnyvale, or Seattle, and involves occasional domestic and international travel, up to 10% of the time. Key job responsibilities - Develop and own algorithms for state of charge, state of health, power capability, and remaining useful life, combining physics-based models with data-driven and estimation methods. - Deliver validated reference implementations, test vectors, and accuracy targets that define what production code must achieve. - Design the test plans and data needed to develop and validate algorithms, working with the cell and testing teams to turn lab and field data into model improvements. - Analyze algorithm performance across the deployed fleet, find where models drift or fail, and drive improvements. - Own the accuracy and robustness of battery algorithms, and sign off that production implementations match the validated reference. Provide algorithm evidence for safety certification. A day in the life Your week moves between data, models, and experiments. One day you might be working out why a health estimate drifts on cells that have aged in the field, and the next deciding which model structure holds accuracy at cold temperatures. You could be designing a test with the cell team to expose a behavior your model misses, or reviewing an implementation with an applied scientist to confirm that what ships matches what you validated. You will regularly share results with software, systems, and cell leaders, and your findings will shape decisions well beyond the algorithm itself. About the team We are building Amazon's energy storage capability, providing power for advanced technologies while contributing to a stable grid. Our product is highly connected, yet secure and resilient by design. We own it end to end, from software, ML, and controls through system design to cell selection and supply, and on to a safety-certified product in the field. The organization operates like a startup inside Amazon: small, fast-moving, and accountable for our decisions. We work across hardware, software, and science, with suppliers and partners worldwide, and with Amazon infrastructure, procurement, legal, and finance. The organization is at an early stage and growing quickly. You will be among the first algorithm hires, so you will help shape how we design, build, certify, and ship, with a direct line of sight to the product and business decisions your work informs. This is a dynamic role that will regularly present new challenges as the product and organization evolve. - Master's degree in electrical engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, applied mathematics, or a related field. - 8+ years of experience developing battery algorithms or battery models in industry or research with a Master's degree, or 5+ years with a PhD. - Extensive experience launching battery products with leading automotive or grid storage OEMs may be considered in place of some of this experience. - Experience developing state of charge or state of health estimation algorithms for lithium-ion batteries, including building equivalent circuit models and using methods such as Kalman filtering or data-driven models. - Experience validating battery algorithms against laboratory and field data. - Expert proficiency in Python for building and validating battery models, and the ability to prototype algorithms in C. - Familiarity with automotive or battery energy storage system (BESS) safety standards, such as ISO 26262, UL 1973, or UL 9540A. - PhD in electrical engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, applied mathematics, or a related field. - Experience building physics-based electrochemical models, such as the Doyle-Fuller-Newman (DFN) or single particle model (SPM) or other advanced battery models, and with lithium-ion aging mechanisms. - Experience with lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, including state of charge estimation across the flat voltage plateau and hysteresis. - Familiarity with lithium-ion failure modes and abuse hazards, such as overcharge, internal short, and thermal runaway, and experience developing algorithms to detect them. - Experience designing battery test protocols, such as hybrid pulse power characterization (HPPC), drive or duty cycles, and impedance spectroscopy. - Experience making technical trade-offs on a safety-critical product, where certification and field reliability constrain cost and schedule. - Comfortable making decisions with incomplete information, and effective across cultures, companies, and time zones. jobs.title: Senior Context Fusion AI Engineer - Autonomous Vehicles
jobs.location: US, CA, Santa Clara US, NV, Remote US, WA, Redmond US, WA, Seattle
jobs.jd: We are looking for a strong engineer to join the DRIVE Road Structure / Online Mapping / Context Fusion team. In this role, you will help craft and guide the future of our L3/L4 autonomous-driving solution by building a complete, learned 3D/4D world model that fuses navigation, ego-motion, perception, and sensor signals. You will work closely with perception, prediction, planning, and simulation teams to deliver a world representation that is complete, temporally consistent, uncertainty-aware, and robust enough to drive through the most challenging roads and intersections in L3/L4 autonomy level. This role is central to our vision for AV: developing a shared multimodal scene representation that can jointly support road understanding, 3D object and occupancy perception, motion prediction, and route-conditioned planning. Are you interested in inventing human-level AI for navigation in the unconstrained world under any conditions? If so, join us ! What You'll Be Doing: Design and develop learning-based, multimodal sensor-fusion systems that transform synchronized sensor history, ego-motion, navigation context, and driving context into a unified spatiotemporal world representation. Build architectures that jointly reason over camera, LiDAR, radar, and vehicle-state inputs, with appropriate handling of calibration, synchronization, coordinate transforms, sensor latency, and uncertainty. Develop end-to-end and multi-task models that produce driving-relevant outputs from a shared scene representation, including; road graph elements such as lanes, boundaries, crosswalks, and traffic controls; semantic scene understanding; occupancy and free-space representations, including uncertain and occluded regions; Develop scalable multimodal fusion architectures, including Transformer-based early, late, and hierarchical fusion; BEV, point/voxel, and image-based representations; temporal context aggregation; and cross-modal attention. Create training, fine-tuning, and evaluation pipelines for large-scale multimodal datasets. Define multi-task objectives and metrics that balance perception quality, geometric consistency, prediction accuracy, latency, and safety-critical behavior. Investigate foundation-model approaches for autonomous driving, including vision-language models, multimodal pre-training, representation learning, and efficient deployment of learned world models. Work closely with perception, mapping, prediction, planning, simulation, data, and embedded-software teams to convert research advances into robust, production-quality AV systems. Develop systematic analysis and debugging tools for model failures, cross-sensor disagreement, long-tail scenarios, distribution shift, and regressions in closed-loop simulation and on-road evaluation. What We Need To See: BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience. 8+ years of experience, with at least 2+ years in the AV or robotics industry and 2+ years of leadership experience in a technically area Strong experience developing production-quality sensor-fusion, perception, state-estimation, or autonomous-driving systems. Demonstrated experience with learning-based multimodal perception or fusion involving two or more cameras, LiDAR, radar, map, navigation, and ego-motion signals. Solid understanding of 3D geometry, coordinate frames, calibration, temporal synchronization, ego-motion compensation, tracking, uncertainty estimation, and sensor failure modes. Experience with deep-learning methods for 3D perception, lego-context scene representation, occupancy/occlusion prediction, semantic segmentation, object detection/tracking, motion prediction, or planning. Strong C++ and Python programming skills, with hands-on experience developing, training, and optimizing deep-learning models in PyTorch. Experience with CUDA, distributed training, mixed-precision techniques, and efficient GPU inference using NVIDIA software and hardware is highly valued. Experience with Transformer, VLM, or multimodal foundation-model architectures, including pre-training, fine-tuning, distillation, quantization, or efficient inference. Experience training and evaluating models at scale, including distributed training, dataset curation, offline evaluation, simulation-based validation, and production monitoring. Ability to work across research and engineering boundaries: turn an ambiguous AV problem into measurable technical objectives, build the solution, and drive it to deployment. Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd: Experience building multi-task driving models that jointly predict perception, road structure, occupancy, motion, and/or trajectories from shared multimodal features. Experience with Transformer, VLM, or multimodal foundation-model architectures, including pre-training, fine-tuning, distillation, quantization, or efficient inference. Experience with BEV, point-cloud/voxel, neural scene representation, 3D reconstruction, occupancy-flow, or spatiotemporal world-model methods. Publications or open-source contributions in computer vision, robotics, machine learning, 3D perception, multimodal learning, or autonomous driving. jobs.jd: About Quilter At Quilter, we are helping electrical engineers save time and accomplish more by automating the tedious and time-consuming task of designing printed circuit boards (PCBs). Our small team is composed of experts in electrical engineering, electromagnetic simulation, ML/AI, and high-performance computing (HPC). We are inventing and leveraging novel techniques to solve the decades-old problem of automating circuit board design where today hundreds of billions of dollars are spent. We have raised $25 million in Series B funding from some of the very best and are charging full-speed toward our goal. No matter where we come from, we're united by a common vision for the future and a core set of values we think will get us there: Focus on the mission Build great things that help humans Demonstrate grit Never stop learning Pursue excellence We're looking for a Senior ML Engineer to join Quilter's Placer Team and help us build the AI that automates component placement on PCBs. The Role The Placer is responsible for automated component placement on PCBs. This role spans the full lifecycle: research, prototyping, productionization, and maintenance. You'll work across optimization, machine learning, and geometric deep learning on a hard, real-world combinatorial problem. This is a fully distributed team. We expect high autonomy and high ownership. What Youʼll Do Own problems end-to-end from exploratory R&D through production-hardened, maintainable systems Develop and extend GPU-accelerated code in PyTorch and CUDA C++ Work across a broad modeling landscape including RL, graph neural networks, black-box/classical optimization, and generative modeling Formulate objectives, model constraints, and debug numerical behavior in the stack Contribute to technical direction and research strategy alongside senior teammates What Weʼre Looking For 5+ years of industry experience in ML, optimization, or a related field Strong fundamentals in machine learning and optimization Production PyTorch experience Demonstrated ability to work across research and production codebases Comfort operating with high autonomy in ambiguous problem spaces Strong communication and collaboration skills Preferred 5–7 years of industry experience (Staff-level appointment may be considered) CUDA C++ experience Background in any combination of: reinforcement learning, geometric deep learning, graph neural networks, multi-objective optimization, combinatorial optimization Please note : We are an equal opportunity employer. At this time, we are focused on hiring primarily within the US, with occasional exception to accommodate exceptional talent. What we offer: Interesting and challenging work Competitive salary and equity benefits Health, dental, and vision insurance Regular team events and offsites (~4x / year) Unlimited paid time off Paid parental leave Want to learn more about Quilter, our vision, and our investors?
